Subject: Finova: Post-call - Performance SLOs & Regional Routing

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the call today — great overview of Finova's use case. Per our discussion, I'm following up with a concise list of SLO/traffic questions so Dev and I can size the right routing and capacity approach (hosted vs dedicated) and propose a mutual action plan.

Quick asks (can you reply inline?):
- Target latency SLOs (p95) by region (US / EU / APAC) — what are your SLA targets for customer-facing latency?
- Expected peak concurrency and average QPS (approx) for generation requests (include typical tokens per response)
- Do you need streaming partial responses/real-time token streaming? If yes, any max token-rate expectations?
- Data residency constraints: do EU requests need to stay in EU (both processing + logs)? Any APAC residency requirements?
- Expected regional traffic split (%% by region) during peak and steady state

Attachments for context: redwood-slo-template.xlsx (SLO worksheet + example config). Also linking our SLO guidance: https://redwood-inference.com/docs/slo-guidance

Suggested next steps:
1) You reply with the bullets above (or attach a small traffic spreadsheet)
2) We schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev (30–45m) to review routing/pinning and streaming behavior
3) Redwood will produce 2 options: (A) Hosted + smart-regional routing with EU data pinning, (B) Dedicated regional pools (US/EU/APAC) with predictable latency and capacity pricing

I'll aim to get options back within 3 business days after the technical deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below and attached a CSV with our rough traffic estimates (finova_traffic_estimates.csv).

- Latency SLOs (p95):
  - US: 200 ms
  - EU: 300 ms
  - APAC: 450 ms (we understand higher latency in APAC is expected)
- Peak concurrency: ~1,200 concurrent generation sessions during peak (concurrent users initiating requests)
- Average QPS: ~40 sustained, with spikes to ~75 QPS for short bursts (1–5 min)
- Tokens per response: typically 350–600 tokens; some product flows hit 1,000 tokens (rare, <5% of calls)
- Streaming: yes — we need partial token streaming for the main product signup flow (UX depends on first tokens arriving within ~150–200ms)
- Token-rate for streaming: we don't have a strict tokens/sec target but expect steady streams of ~20–30 tokens/sec for long responses
- Data residency: EU customer data (including logs and any persisted KV/cache entries tied to EU customers) must stay in EU. APAC data residency preferred but negotiable for initial POC if routed to APAC region; long-term requirement could be mandatory depending on regulator feedback.
- Regional distribution (peak): US 60%, EU 30%, APAC 10%

Procurement timeline: aiming for POC in April, production Q4. We're evaluating whether Dedicated regional pools are necessary vs Hosted with strong EU pinning. Can you include cost delta estimates in the options?

Cheers,
Samir
Head of Integrations, Finova

Hi Samir / Marissa — looping in technical details from our side after reviewing the numbers. Attaching a short options PDF (regional-routing-options.pdf).

High-level feasibility notes:
- Latency: Achievable. To meet p95=200ms US and 300ms EU for 350–600 token responses at your concurrency, we recommend either (A) Dedicated regional pools sized for peak concurrency, or (B) Hosted with strong per-tenant regional pinning + pre-warmed vCPU/GPU pools. Hosted can meet targets for typical traffic patterns but has higher variance during global bursts.
- Streaming: Fully supported. Streaming latency (first-token) depends on network hop + model cold-start. We can meet ~150ms first-token in US with pre-warmed instances and tuned batching (small micro-batches for streaming flows). For EU, expect 200–300ms first-token depending on region and network path.
- Batching and throughput: Continuous batching with target batch sizes will improve GPU utilization. For streaming flows, we recommend a per-route low-latency batching profile (flush after X ms / Y tokens) to maintain first-token constraints.
- KV cache: We can pin KV/cache to region for residency. For EU-only residency, all cache writes/read route to EU pools; cross-region fallback is configurable but will be disabled unless authorized.
- Routing: Options
  1) Three Dedicated pools (US/EU/APAC) — simplest latency isolation and easiest to guarantee SLOs + residency. Predictable monthly commit pricing.
  2) Hosted + Regional Pinning — lower upfront cost, uses smart-routing to keep EU traffic in EU; fallbacks to other regions only on explicit policy. Slightly less deterministic under extreme global bursts.
  3) Hybrid — Dedicated EU (to satisfy regulated customers) + Hosted for US/APAC to reduce cost.
- Failover & fallbacks: We can configure failovers to model variants with graceful degradation (smaller context length, quantized variants) to keep services online during saturation.
- Networking: If Finova requires strict data residency, we recommend a direct interconnect or private VPC peering for EU region to avoid egress through third-party regions. This reduces tail latency and simplifies audit trails.

Open questions for sizing: please confirm in-flight invocation split vs idle sessions and share your RPS distribution by minute if available. That will help us produce concrete pool sizes and cost numbers.

Next suggested actions:
1) Schedule a 45m architecture deep-dive (Dev + one infra engineer) — Marissa, can you coordinate?
2) We'll produce options with estimated costs and a recommended POC configuration (time to POC and runbook).

Thanks,
